title: Subnet a host address
prompt: A host has the IPv4 address 192.168.10.77 with the prefix /26. Work out the subnet it belongs to.

fields.label: Usable host addresses in the subnet

explanation: /26 leaves 6 host bits, so each subnet has 2^6 = 64 addresses and the subnets start at .0, .64, .128 and .192. Address .77 falls in the block .64 to .127: the first address is the network address and the last is the broadcast address. Usable hosts = 64 - 2 = 62.

title: Average waiting time
prompt: Four processes arrive at time 0 in the order P1, P2, P3, P4 with CPU burst times of 6, 8, 7 and 3 ms. Calculate the average waiting time under each scheduling policy.
explanation: FCFS runs them in arrival order, so the waits are 0, 6, 14 and 21 ms: (0 + 6 + 14 + 21) / 4 = 10.25. SJF runs the shortest first (3, 6, 7, 8), so the waits are 0, 3, 9 and 16 ms: 28 / 4 = 7. SJF gives the minimum average waiting time.

title: Page faults
prompt: A process references pages in this order: 7 0 1 2 0 3 0 4 2 3 0 3 2. Memory has 3 frames, all empty at the start. Count the page faults for each replacement policy.
explanation: Every reference to a page that is not in a frame is a fault, including the first three. FIFO evicts the page that was loaded earliest and produces 10 faults. LRU evicts the page that was used least recently and produces 9 faults. Trace the frames step by step to check.

title: RAID usable capacity
prompt: A storage array has six 4 TB disks. Give the usable capacity for each RAID level.
explanation: RAID 0 stripes with no redundancy, so all 6 disks count: 24 TB. RAID 1+0 mirrors every disk, so half is usable: 12 TB. RAID 5 uses one disk of parity: 5 x 4 = 20 TB. RAID 6 uses two disks of parity: 4 x 4 = 16 TB.

title: System availability
prompt: A service needs a web server (availability 99.9%) and a database server (availability 99.5%) to both be running. Separately, a pair of application servers, each 99% available, is set up so that either one can carry the service.

fields.label: Availability of web and database in series (%)

explanation: In series both must work, so multiply: 0.999 x 0.995 = 0.994005, about 99.40%. With redundancy the pair fails only if both fail: 1 - (0.01 x 0.01) = 0.9999, or 99.99%. A year has 8,760 hours, and 0.1% of that is 8.76 hours.

title: RSA with small numbers
prompt: Use RSA with the primes p = 3 and q = 11 and the public exponent e = 3.
explanation: n = p x q = 33. phi(n) = (p - 1)(q - 1) = 2 x 10 = 20. d is the inverse of e modulo 20: 3 x 7 = 21, which leaves remainder 1, so d = 7. Encryption is m^e mod n: 4^3 = 64, and 64 mod 33 = 31.

title: Earned value analysis
prompt: A project has a budget at completion (BAC) of 100,000. At the end of month 5 it was planned to be 50% complete. It is actually 40% complete and has cost 45,000 so far.

title: Critical path
prompt: A project has these activities (duration in days, predecessors): A (3, none), B (4, A), C (2, A), D (5, B), E (6, C), F (2, D and E).

fields.label: Critical path, as letters such as ACEF

explanation: There are two paths. A-B-D-F takes 3 + 4 + 5 + 2 = 14 days and A-C-E-F takes 3 + 2 + 6 + 2 = 13 days. The longest path is the critical path, so the project takes 14 days. Activities C and E can slip by 14 - 13 = 1 day without delaying the project.

title: Three-point estimate
prompt: An activity is estimated at 4 days in the optimistic case, 7 days most likely and 16 days in the pessimistic case. Use the PERT formulas.
explanation: Expected = (O + 4M + P) / 6 = (4 + 28 + 16) / 6 = 8 days. Standard deviation = (P - O) / 6 = (16 - 4) / 6 = 2 days.

title: Payback period and ROI
prompt: A system costs 200,000 to build and returns a net benefit of 80,000 at the end of each year for 4 years. Ignore the time value of money.
explanation: The cumulative benefit reaches 200,000 after 200,000 / 80,000 = 2.5 years. Total benefit over 4 years is 320,000, so ROI = (320,000 - 200,000) / 200,000 = 60%.
